summary: Bounded auth set-token's stdin read so an inherited-but-idle stdin can no longer hang the command indefinitely.
reason: Round 2 removed the positional-token path and made stdin the only input for auth set-token, using io.ReadAll(cmd.InOrStdin()). Greptile's round-3 re-review (score 4/5, up from 1/5) confirmed the prior MCP auth/TLS, snapshot-label, and positional-token findings resolved, but flagged that io.ReadAll blocks until EOF, so an invocation that inherits an open stdin with nothing forthcoming (a bare interactive run with nothing typed, or a parent process that never writes or closes its end of a pipe) hangs forever. Replaced the read with readStdinTokenLine: a single-line bufio.Scanner read racing a 60s timeout via a goroutine + select. Piped/redirected input (the documented usage) still resolves as soon as the line is available; an idle stdin now fails with a clear, actionable error after 60s instead of hanging.
validated_outcome: Verified with a throwaway test (removed before commit): a never-written, never-closed io.Pipe times out in ~1s against a 1s bound and returns an error; a pipe with one line written returns immediately. End-to-end: `echo faketoken | auth set-token --json` still completes in well under a second. go build/vet/gofmt clean; existing pre-existing unrelated test failure unchanged.
